Finding: the earlier accepted UseMultiTenant mutation establishes that UseMultiTenant is not what protects the Billing HTTP read path; its tenant read guarantee travels through the Wolverine/bus-tenant chain rather than that HTTP middleware. These two prescribed mutations, however, both left the foreign read denied, so they do not establish which element of that chain is presently load-bearing and must not be used to claim that the BaseDbContext lazy fallback or the TenantMessageBusMiddleware assignment alone protects this probe. The next single element to test is AmbientTenantEnvelopeRule.Modify's assignment of Envelope.TenantId from TenantPropagationContext, because it can stamp the in-process GetInvoiceQuery after the HTTP bus middleware and would explain why neutralising bus.TenantId did not change the observed result.

implementation-result.remaining-risks: Neither prescribed mutation made a foreign invoice readable. Therefore the exact current protection mechanism is not proven by these experiments; the recommended next isolated mutation is AmbientTenantEnvelopeRule.Modify's Envelope.TenantId stamping, for the stated causal reason. Existing package and analyzer warnings (including NU1903 for SSH.NET) were emitted by the focused test runs and are outside this evidence-only task.
